coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Find the missing number
coding.question: You are given N-1 distinct integers. They are all the numbers from 1 to N in some order, except that exactly one number is missing. Find the missing number.
coding.input_format:
First line: N.
Second line: N-1 space-separated integers.
coding.constraints: 2 <= N <= 100000. Every given number is between 1 and N and appears once.
coding.starter_code:
n = int(input())
nums = list(map(int, input().split()))
# TODO: write your logic here
print(0)
coding.solution:
n = int(input())
nums = list(map(int, input().split()))
print(n * (n + 1) // 2 - sum(nums))
hints: The sum of 1 to N is N*(N+1)/2.
Subtract the sum of the given numbers from it.
coding.explanation: The numbers 1 to N add up to N*(N+1)/2. Subtracting the sum of the given N-1 numbers leaves the missing one. O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
coding.label: Candidate-reported

coding.explanation: Loop over the string once and print each character with ord(ch). O(n) time.

coding.title: Inverted star pyramid
coding.question: Print an inverted full pyramid of stars with N rows. The first row has 2N-1 stars and no leading spaces. Each next row has one more leading space and two fewer stars, so the last row has N-1 leading spaces and a single star. Do not print spaces after the stars.

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Run-length compression
coding.question: Compress a string of lowercase letters by replacing every run of the same letter with the letter followed by the length of the run. For example, aaabccdddd becomes a3b1c2d4. A run is a maximal block of equal letters next to each other, so aabaa becomes a2b1a2.
coding.input_format: One line: a string S of lowercase letters.
coding.starter_code:
s = input().strip()
# TODO: write your logic here
print(s)
coding.solution:
s = input().strip()
out = []
i = 0
while i < len(s):
    j = i
    while j < len(s) and s[j] == s[i]:
        j += 1
    out.append(s[i] + str(j - i))
    i = j
print("".join(out))
hints: Walk through the string with two pointers: i marks the start of a run, j moves until the letter changes.
coding.explanation: Scan once. For each run starting at i, move j forward while the letter is the same, then append the letter and j - i. O(n) time.
coding.label: AI practice
coding.source_note: Written for practice on Deloitte's reported coding topics

coding.input_format:

Line 2: n words (lowercase letters) separated by spaces.
coding.output_format: One line: two integers, the number of groups and the size of the largest group.

3 3

coding.starter_code:
import sys
d = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(d[0]); words = d[1:1 + n]
# TODO: group words by their sorted letters
print(0, 0)
coding.solution:
import sys
d = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(d[0]); words = d[1:1 + n]
groups = {}
for w in words:
    key = "".join(sorted(w))          # anagrams share the same sorted letters
    groups[key] = groups.get(key, 0) + 1
print(len(groups), max(groups.values()))
hints: Sort the letters of a word: all anagrams give the same sorted string.
Use that sorted string as a dictionary key and count.
coding.explanation: Map each word to its sorted letters and count words per key in a dictionary. The number of keys is the number of groups. O(n * L log L) for n words of length L.

coding.title: Longest palindromic substring
coding.question: Given a string S of lowercase letters, find its longest substring that reads the same forwards and backwards. A substring is a continuous part of the string. If several palindromic substrings have the same maximum length, print the one that starts first (leftmost).
coding.starter_code:
s = input().strip()
# TODO: write your logic here
print(s[0])
hints: Every palindrome has a centre: one letter (odd length) or the gap between two letters (even length).
Expand outwards from each centre while the two ends match.
coding.explanation: Try all 2N-1 centres and expand while the characters on both sides match, keeping the longest (leftmost on ties). O(N^2) time and O(1) extra space, fine for N = 1000.

coding.title: Longest subarray with sum K
coding.question: Given an array of N integers (they can be negative or zero) and a number K, find the length of the longest continuous subarray whose elements add up to exactly K. If no such subarray exists, print 0.
coding.input_format:
First line: N and K.
Second line: N space-separated integers.
coding.output_format: Print the length of the longest subarray with sum K, or 0.
coding.starter_code:
n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
# TODO: write your logic here
print(0)
hints: The sum of a[l..r] equals prefix[r] - prefix[l-1].
Store the first index where each prefix sum appears; a sliding window does not work with negatives.
coding.explanation: Keep a running prefix sum and a dictionary of the first index where each prefix value appeared (0 at index -1). At index i, if prefix - K was seen at index j, the subarray j+1..i sums to K. O(n) time and O(n) space.

    a = b
